text:
cheng: Heads up — in the last 2h we saw ~18 tiny-pod evictions in us-east1-b that look like a packing ripple after a warm-pool scale event. Pods are small (<0.5 GPU) and keep bouncing between nodes.

sara: Saw the charts. eviction-rate spiked at 18:12 UTC, correlated with a fleet resize + rack-level NIC flaps earlier. suspect thin-slot fragmentation + latebind scheduling.

infra-bot: alert: GPU_POD_EVICTION spike detected in cluster-prod/us-east1-b (18 events, 2h). Top reason: Preempted -> NodePressure/Kubelet eviction probe.

alex: timeline: autoscaler added 6 nodes at ~18:05, warmpool drained and then backfilled. During backfill, binpacking pushed small pods onto partially-used GPUs -> KV-cache mismatch and then teeny preempts.

cheng: Logs show many pods have nodeAffinity soft-prefer but also tolerate a taint we set last week `rack:isolated:NoSchedule` as a stopgap. That combination + late node readiness is making scheduler pick suboptimal nodes.

kyle: Cost note: the small-pod churn is increasing tokenized billing for Dedicated customers because we pay GPU uptime on the node even if pods are tiny. If churn continues, monthly delta could be ~3-6% on US fleet.

ops-lead: Proposal A: reduce warm-pool shrink aggression and add a soft-affinity boost for `gpu-utilization < 0.25` to prefer co-locating tiny pods on same node. Proposal B: bump lease expiry to 45s so KV warming finishes before scheduling.

sara: I'm +1 on increasing lease expiry temporarily for the canary AZ. We should test for latency regressions. Also want to try a scheduler scoring tweak: penalize cross-rack placement for tiny pods (score -150) while keeping large jobs unaffected.

cheng: Quick k8s scheduler patch snippet to test (canary):
```yaml
- name: PreferLocalTinyPods
  type: Score
  weight: 30
  params:
    predicate: "pod.gpuRequest < 0.5"
    scoring: "preferredLocality"
    penalty: 150
```

alex: Quick telemetry: here's the query I ran (p95 eviction window):
```
count_over_time(kube_pod_eviction_total{cluster="prod",zone="us-east1-b"}[2h])
```
Result: 18 at peak, baseline usually <2.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: started rollout of scheduler-config v2-canary to us-east1-b at 18:45 UTC by sara. (dry-run mode = true)

sara: Running dry-run now. If dry-run looks good for 20m with no new evictions, we'll promote to us-east1-c next.

kyle: Also recommend setting `warmpool_min=2` for the canary AZ to reduce churn during scaling. That will slightly up run-hours but reduce preempt churn.

ops-lead: Action items: (1) canary scheduler scoring + lease bump (sara) (2) set warmpool_min=2 for us-east1-b (cheng) (3) monitor eviction p95 and cost signal (kyle). Triage call in 30m if anything spikes.

cheng: acked. I'll prepare the eviction dashboards and a short oncall playbook snippet for rollbacks.

alex: thanks — ping @sara if we see network retransmits again; that was the other culprit last time.

sara: Will do. If canary shows regressions we revert config and revert warmpool change.

kyle: noted; I'll track monthly cost sim for this change and post numbers tomorrow.

infra-bot: incident-status: monitoring for 1h post-rollout. Notify channel if eviction_count > 5 in 30m.

cheng: closing the loop: canary dry-run stable at +22m, no new evictions. Promoting to us-east1-c in 10m. Will open PR with the scheduler rule if anyone wants to review the exact scoring details.

ops-lead: nice work. :tada:
